newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco area economy seen growing in 1997-98.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco area economy seen growing in 1997-98.

text.p: The San Francisco Bay area can expect nearly 60,000 new jobs and a 2.0 percent increase in household income during 1997, economists at the Association of Bay Area Governments said on Wednesday.

Association researchers also forecast a 9.0 percent increase in retail sales for the nine-county region in the new year. The increase is expected to decline only slightly in 1998, with anticipated growth of almost 8.0 percent.

"High-tech manufacturing is leading the economic growth for the Bay Area," Paul Fassinger, the association's research director, said. "Although computer software and Internet services are certainly on the rise, almost 25 percent of the economic growth in this region during 1996 can be attributed to high-tech manufacturing."
The association, however, forecast a gradual increase in inflation, which came in at 2.3 percent for 1996, and was expected to rise to 2.8 percent in 1997 and 3.0 percent in 1998.
The association will present its forecast in detail at its economic conference in Oakland later on Wednesday.
